info.title: Follow-up CRM API
info.description:
REST API for the Lead Generation & Follow-up Android app.

**Auth:** call `POST /api/auth/login` (demo: `admin@example.com` / `password`), copy the `token`, click **Authorize** and paste it.

**Dates:** send `YYYY-MM-DD` dates and `HH:MM` (24h) times; responses include ISO-8601 timestamps plus separate date/time fields.

**Follow-ups:** a lead has at most one *pending* follow-up (its next follow-up). Completed follow-ups form the lead's timeline.

post.summary: Check whether a website responds (not saved)
post.description:
Optional, polite check: validates the URL, refuses localhost/private addresses, reads robots.txt first, follows up to 5 redirects, handles SSL errors and uses short timeouts. Limited to 10 checks per minute.

**A failed check never means the website does not exist.**

parameters.description: Status of the linked CRM lead

post.description:
Saves the researched business and (unless `save_to_crm=false`) creates a CRM lead in the existing leads table:

| Business field | CRM lead field |
|---|---|
| Business name | company |
| Contact person (or business name) | name |
| Phone | mobile |
| Email | email |
| — | source = `Business Finder` |
| Category, location, website | appended to notes |
| — | status `New`, priority `Medium` (overridable) |

Send `next_followup_date` / `next_followup_time` to schedule the first call through the existing follow-up system. A phone number already used by one of your CRM leads returns **409** with the existing lead; resend with `on_duplicate=link` to attach to it.

post.summary: Save a researched business to the CRM
post.description: Creates the CRM lead (same mapping as Add Business to CRM) and optionally schedules the first call. 409 when already saved or when the phone belongs to another lead (use on_duplicate=link).

The salesperson confirms the details. Nothing is verified automatically.

`Do not contact` cancels the pending follow-up of the linked CRM lead and blocks new ones; the record is left out of exports.

notes.example: Spoke to reception, owner available after 5 pm

post.summary: Check the business website and store the result
post.description: Uses the saved website (or `url`, which is then saved). The website status is changed only when the site clearly responds (→ Website available); otherwise the result is stored and the salesperson decides.

get.summary: Export businesses as CSV, Excel or PDF
get.description:
Only your own records. Do-not-contact records are excluded unless `include_do_not_contact=1`.

Presets (`scope`): `all`, `verified_contacts`, `no_website` (marked No website found after research), `followups` (saved leads with a scheduled call).
Selected records: `ids[]=1&ids[]=5`. All list filters also apply. PDF is limited to 1000 records.

post.summary: Mark a follow-up completed and schedule the next one automatically
post.description:
Records the call outcome. Unless `schedule_next=false` or an explicit next date is sent, the next follow-up is auto-scheduled:

| Status after call | Next follow-up |
|---|---|
| Not Answered / Callback | +1 day |
| Interested | +1 day (High), +3 (Medium), +5 (Low) |
| Closed | none |

The original time of day is kept and Sundays are skipped.

post.summary: Import leads from Excel (.xlsx) or CSV
post.description:
First row must be a header. Required column: **Customer Name**. Optional: ID, Mobile Number, Email, Company Name, Lead Source, Status, Priority, Notes, Next Follow-up Date, Next Follow-up Time.

Rows matching an existing lead by ID or mobile number update it; others are created. Use the export file as a template.
